Consult Summary:
- Patient presents with ~5 days of dry cough and nasal discharge (green), with subjective hot/c chilly sensations; no shortness of breath, chest pain, or hemoptysis.
- History of diabetes and hypertension on metformin and lisinopril; currently managing symptoms with OTC lemon sips; clinician advises temperature monitoring, red-flag precautions, and routine GP follow-up.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Acute respiratory symptoms for ~5 days: dry cough (approx. every 20–30 minutes) and nasal discharge; green nasal discharge; no sputum production, no fever measurement provided, no chest pain, no shortness of breath.
- Associated symptoms: hot and chilly sensations; fatigability not prominent; able to maintain fluids and oral intake; no vomiting or diarrhea currently.
- Exam/system review: No vitals or physical exam findings documented.
- Social/Medications/Exam findings: Diabetes mellitus and hypertension; on metformin and lisinopril. Weight 65 kg, height 5'5". Alcohol use: occasional. Lives with partner and dog. No home glucose monitoring documented.
- Differential/Impression: Suspected acute viral or chest infection/inflammatory process; clinician notes infection in the chest suspected and virus is common cause.
- Additional notes: Green nasal discharge; no blood in urine/nose; no rhinorrhea with epistaxis reported.

Issue 2:
- Chronic conditions: Diabetes mellitus and hypertension.
- Timeline: Diabetic and hypertensive history; last diabetes-related blood test ~3 weeks ago and reported as normal; last blood pressure check not documented.
- Medications: Metformin; Lisinopril (dose not clearly documented beyond patient reporting “200”); no home glucose monitoring equipment reported.
- Social/Exam findings: Weight stable; BMI around 22.8; living with partner and dog; works as office manager; alcohol use occasional.
- Differential/Impression: Chronic disease management ongoing; no acute hypertensive crisis or hypoglycemia reported.
- Plan considerations: Maintain routine GP follow-up for BP and diabetes management; ensure diabetes management and BP monitoring continue with the primary care provider.

Plan:
- Advise patient to obtain a thermometer and monitor temperature; reassess if fever persists or peaks above 37.5–38 C, if cough worsens, if there is shortness of breath, chest pain, or coughing up blood.
- Acknowledge most respiratory infections are viral and self-limiting; antibiotics may be considered if not improving or if concerns arise.
- Continue symptomatic care (lemon sips as used); avoid using additional paracetamol-containing products with Lemsip; daytime cough syrup discouraged unless sleep is significantly affected, in which case limited use is acceptable.
- Emphasize diabetes and hypertension follow-up with GP; ensure monitoring and routine labs as previously advised; no home blood glucose monitoring reported.
- Return visit or re-contact if red flags develop or symptoms fail to improve.
